facts.value: `grI2_StageData` publishes the callback and fourteen-entry joint tables. Startup requests Ground objects 0 and 2, then disables the fourteen listed collision joints. Later timers request objects 3, 4, 15, and 1. Each requested ID indexes `grI2_StageCallbacks`; the factory installs a present callback3 into `Ground.x1C_callback`, invokes a present initializer synchronously, and schedules a present process at priority 4. It does not consume callback1 in this setup path.

facts.value: Runs a fixed local sequence: cache parameters, clear startup b4, set b5, configure maps 0 and 2, disable the fourteen listed collision joints, initialize camera range before blast-zone range, and set the two camera constants. Nullable map-creation results are ignored, so a reported missing object does not stop subsequent startup calls. If authored markers are unavailable, the shared routines use Inishie2 camera bounds left/right -200/200 and bottom/top -60/200 with offset (0,130), and blast-zone bounds left/right -300/300 and bottom/top -160/300. Authored blast coordinates are normalized using the camera offsets established first.

facts.value: Each channel is independently armed. An armed channel samples and decrements its signed timer; a saved value of zero becomes -1 without firing, and the next update fires. Successful children begin a separate delayed-activation lifecycle and eventually rearm their matching parent channel on animation completion. Failed creation leaves the channel disarmed with no local retry.

facts.value: When the animation predicate succeeds, the entry branch classifies `xD8.x + xCC.x` against camera bounds and clears entry only inside the interval; it does not increment xCA, including on the boundary that clears entry. On subsequent non-entry boundaries, while departure has not been committed, xCA values below 2 force direction alternation; later boundaries either commit to departure outside the camera or use the configured weights to decide reversal inside. The non-entry branch increments xCA even after departure is committed. Every successful animation-boundary path selects an animation and rebases JObj 0 to the accumulated position; the other path samples JObj 1 into xCC. The source assigns boundary result 2 or 1 into xC8_flags.b3 without establishing a three-state animation domain here. The caller removes the object only after departure is enabled and its world position crosses a horizontal blast-zone edge.

facts.rationale: Corrects startup collision polarity and preserves the cross-object and cross-file lifetimes rather than reducing them to generic registration and handoff.
facts.value: The stage framework uses `grI2_StageData` and its ID-indexed callback table. Startup caches the externally supplied Yakumono parameter pointer, configures maps 0 and 2, and disables the fourteen listed collision joints. Controller callbacks consume shared timing and spawn parameters to attempt transient maps 3, 4, 15 and 1, disarm their channels, and attach parent backlinks only on successful creation. Child callbacks use those backlinks to restore randomized parent delays before destruction. Birdo additionally retains a Ground owner in its separately simulated Kyasarin item; item damage notifies collision removal, while item destruction notifies Ground teardown and recurrence. The traveling platform accumulates animation displacement and requires departure plus a horizontal blast-zone crossing before removal.
